Done. Here's what I changed and why, based on the Next.js 16 canary docs in node_modules/next/dist/docs/.

## What changed

next.config.ts — enabled partialPrefetching: true alongside the existing cacheComponents: true. This switches <Link> from the legacy full prefetch to the per-route App Shell model, and is required for the prefetch() function to have any effect.

app/product/page.tsx — moved related products behind await prefetch() (from next/cache) inside a <Suspense> boundary:
- The page is now a sync function that renders the static shell (h1, description, section heading) plus a <Suspense> fallback.
- A new async RelatedProducts child component awaits prefetch() before calling getRelatedProducts().
- getRelatedProducts() keeps its 'use cache' + cacheLife('hours') directive (it's called below prefetch(), which the docs require — awaiting prefetch() inside a cached scope is not allowed).

app/page.tsx — set prefetch={true} on the featured-product <Link>.

## How it satisfies the request

The route now renders in three stages (per the prefetch() / navigation() docs):

1. App Shell (what every default <Link> prefetches): the static product heading, description, and the "Loading related products…" fallback. Related products are excluded — await prefetch() defers everything below it out of the shell, so a default prefetch never generates them.
2. Per-link prefetch (<Link prefetch={true}>): the featured-product link opts in, so the router resolves the deferred related-products subtree before the click. They're ready immediately on navigation from that link.
3. Navigation: covers anything not resolved above (e.g., if the per-link prefetch hasn't completed).

I used prefetch() rather than navigation() deliberately: navigation() would exclude related products from per-link prefetches too, so they'd only render after the click. prefetch() keeps them out of the default App Shell but lets the prefetch={true} featured link resolve them ahead of time — exactly "out of the default prefetch, ready immediately from the featured link."

## Verification

- npm run build → exit 0. Output confirms "Cache Components enabled" and "Partial Prefetching enabled"; /product prerenders static with Revalidate 1h / Expire 1d (matching cacheLife('hours')). TypeScript passes.
- Dev server smoke test: GET / → 200, GET /product → 200. On direct load (where prefetch() has no effect, per docs), the HTML streams in both the Suspense fallback and the resolved "Compact Widget" content.

One thing to note: prefetch={true} costs a server invocation per visible link into the route. Here there's a single featured link, so that's fine. If many links into /product appear at once later, prefer hover-triggered prefetching instead of prefetch={true} on each.

20 	Prefetching downloads a route's JavaScript, CSS, and RSC payload before the user navigates to it, so the router can render the next route without waiting for a round trip. The [Prefetching guide](/docs/app/guides/prefetching) covers what the App Router prefetches by default.
21 	
22 	With [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) and [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching), a [`<Link>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link) prefetches one reusable [**App Shell**](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) per route by default. Links to the same route reuse that App Shell.
23

30

34 	}
35 	
36 	export default nextConfig
37 	```

42 	
43 	Set `<Link prefetch={true}>` to resolve URL data for that link before navigation. 44

49 	
50 	export default function Home() {

52 	    <nav>

54 	        React
